{'text': 'MS NOW節目主持Jen Psaki於週二詳述《紐約時報》一篇「瘋狂至極」的爆炸性報道，內容關於前司法部顧問Alina Habba，她協助一名委內瑞拉億萬富翁取得總統赦免後，獲得超過5,000萬美元報酬。', 'paragraph_context': 'MS NOW host Jen Psaki on Tuesday chronicled a “crazy insane” bombshell report from The New York Times concerning former Justice Department adviser Alina Habba, who received more than $50 million after helping a Venezuelan billionaire secure a presidential pardon.'}

{'text': 'Psaki於週二《The Briefing》節目中指出：「Habba向《紐約時報》發表聲明否認在赦免事宜中扮演任何角色，並引述其言：『任何暗示我——已經過審查並向司法部申報的——僱傭關係，與取得赦免有任何關聯的說法均屬不實。』」', 'paragraph_context': '“In a statement to the Times, Habba denied any role in the pardon, saying, quote, ‘Any insinuation that my employment — all of which has been vetted and disclosed to the DOJ — had anything to do with securing the pardon is false,’” Psaki noted Tuesday on “The Briefing.”'}

{'text': '「不過，這一連串事件確實相當耐人尋味，對吧？簡直瘋狂。」她說。', 'paragraph_context': '“But man, that sequence of events sure is freakin’ interesting, isn’t it? Crazy insane,” she said.'}

{'text': '《紐約時報》於週二報道，億萬富翁Julio Herrera Velutini向總統Donald Trump尋求赦免美國行賄指控之時，Habba仍任職於司法部，即便這些控罪在2025年一項從寬的認罪協議中已被減輕為一項輕罪選舉財務違規。', 'paragraph_context': 'The Times on Tuesday reported Habba was still at the DOJ when billionaire Julio Herrera Velutini sought a pardon from President Donald Trump for U.S. bribery charges, even after they were reduced in a lenient 2025 plea deal to a misdemeanor campaign finance violation.'}

{'text': 'Psaki賣關子問道：「那麼他做了什麼呢，各位？」她接著說：「根據《紐約時報》的報道，這位委內瑞拉億萬富翁聘請了一名特朗普法律團隊的前成員為他遊說。他的女兒向一個與特朗普有關的超級政治行動委員會捐贈了350萬美元，但他想要的赦免仍未到手。」', 'paragraph_context': '“And so what did he do, everyone?” Psaki teased. “Well, according to the Times, this Venezuelan billionaire hired a former member of Trump’s legal team to lobby for him. His daughter donated $3.5 million to a super PAC tied to Trump, but the pardon he wanted remained elusive.”'}

{'text': '她續說：「後來Herrera家族聘請了特朗普的前私人律師Alina Habba，當時她仍然是特朗普麾下司法部的顧問，各位！這才是最瘋狂的部分！他們開出每年1,000萬美元、為期四年，加上各種花紅的條件給Alina Habba。」', 'paragraph_context': 'She continued, “And then the Herrera family hired Alina Habba, Trump’s former personal lawyer, who was at the time still an adviser at the Trump Justice Department, everyone! This is the crazy part of this! And they offered Alina Habba $10 million a year for four years along with a range of bonuses.”'}

{'text': '《紐約時報》引述其取得的訪問及文件報道，Habba在這四年期間擔任Concord Partners的首席法律顧問，保證獲得超過5,000萬美元報酬。該公司由Velutini的女兒Isabela Herrera於2025年10月成立。', 'paragraph_context': 'The Times reported that Habba was guaranteed more than $50 million over those four years, citing interviews and documents the outlet obtained, as general counsel at Concord Partners, a firm formed in October 2025 by Velutini’s daughter, Isabela Herrera.'}

{'text': 'Psaki說：「她在1月1日正式開始為該公司工作——沒有人知道那公司是做什麼的——而數週後，特朗普便向Velutini頒授全面且無條件的赦免。說到這裡，結果不言而喻。」', 'paragraph_context': '“She formally began her work for that company, which, no one knows what they do, on January 1st,” Psaki said. “And just weeks later, wouldn’t you know it, Trump granted [Velutini] a full and unconditional pardon.”'}

{'text': '為討論該報道所描繪的「極具殺傷力」的情況，Psaki請來前美國聯邦赦免律師Liz Oyer。Oyer直言：「我是說，Jen，這政府的一切都能被收買，包括總統身邊的工作人員。」', 'paragraph_context': 'To discuss the “very damning picture” the report paints, Psaki brought on former U.S. pardon attorney Liz Oyer, who stated bluntly, “I mean, Jen, literally everything in this administration is for sale, including the actual people who work for the president.”'}

{'text': 'Oyer認為，整個案件中最「驚人且具破壞力」的一點是，Velutini最初被指控賄賂政府官員，「目的就是要終止對其名下銀行的調查」。', 'paragraph_context': 'Oyer argued that what is most “stunning and damaging” about this entire case, however, is that Velutini was charged with bribing a government official in the first place, “to shut down an investigation into the bank that he owned.”'}

{'text': '她續說：「如今，他又向另一位政府官員行賄，企圖就首次賄賂脫罪。這正好說明這種腐敗如何自我滋養，形成這種無法無天的惡性循環。」', 'paragraph_context': 'She continued, “And now, he’s bribing another government official to try to get out of trouble for the first bribe. So, it really just illustrates the extent to which this corruption feeds off of itself and creates this vicious cycle of lawlessness.”'}
